patch.value: The linked-file staleness check has no holder-lifecycle partition, so 1,220 links on closed holders warn forever while its worklist truncation hides the actionable subset behind a path count reported as a row count

The linked-file staleness check reports a permanent warning that no agent can act on, and its worklist hides the actionable subset behind a truncation that is advertised with the wrong denominator. Measured 2026-07-29 on the 2,185-item repository tracker.

Scope. 179 distinct linked paths no longer exist on disk: 58 classified deleted, 121 classified moved. Those 179 paths are referenced by 1,220 item-to-path links spread over 472 distinct holder items. All 1,220 links sit on holders with status closed. After the three genuinely stale links on open holders were repaired the same day, the active count is zero and the warning still fires, so it can never be cleared by any action that does not mutate closed items, and mutating closed items reorders changelog sections.

Precedent that already exists in the same command. The dependency_references check faced the identical condition and solved it: it partitions into active_dangling_reference_count, legacy_closed_dangling_reference_count, and legacy_terminal_dangling_reference_count, and reports status ok when the active partition is empty. It is the only one of the nine validate checks that carries lifecycle-partitioned counters, and it is the only one that moved from permanently-warning to green. The files check has no holder-lifecycle dimension at all.

Worklist truncation is worse than it is reported to be. In the default summary mode missing_linked_path_rows holds 40 entries and missing_linked_path_rows_count reports 179. The 40 entries are flattened one per path-and-holder pair and cover only 14 distinct paths. So the denominator is a path count while the numerator is a link count, and a reader who computes 40 of 179 believes it saw 22 percent when it saw 7.8 percent of paths and 3.3 percent of links. Passing --verbose-file-lists changes the row shape from flattened strings to objects that group holders under each path, so the two modes do not merely differ in length, they differ in schema.

The two arrays that would make a repair possible are never joined. missing_linked_path_rows names which items hold each stale path but never names where the file went. missing_linked_path_classifications names where the file went but never names the holder. Both are keyed by path, both are truncated independently at 40 in the default mode, and because rows expand per holder while classifications do not, the two default-mode arrays cover different path sets: 14 paths versus 40. Joining what the default output actually emits yields owner and destination together for at most 14 of 179 paths, with nothing marking the shortfall.

The basename classifier launders malformed links into confident wrong instructions. Three of the 179 stored paths are not paths. Two are comma-joined lists of several paths written as one string, and one carries a note suffix appended after a colon, which is the documented failure mode of passing path-colon-note to a file link flag. The classifier splits on the last path separator, so for the four-path CSV it takes the trailing segment, finds a real file with that basename, and emits a moved classification with a specific destination. A remediation that trusts that output would relink an item to a file it never referenced. A stored link that cannot be a workspace-relative path should be classified as malformed and excluded from move inference entirely.

value.text: Duplicate check before create: pm-j8z6 owns reconciling the linked-file DATA after relocations and its acceptance criteria are about a tracker-only migration, not about how the check reports; pm-6olc95 owns the opposite scoping error on graph audit (active-only coverage that under-reports); pm-2ler is CLOSED and shipped exactly this partition for dependency_references, which is the precedent this item asks the files check to adopt; pm-chyh is CLOSED and covered path anchoring, not staleness reporting. Searched keyword and semantic for validate check gating, active holders, terminal informational, missing linked paths; grepped the corpus for missing_linked_paths holders. No existing item owns the reporting contract of the files check.

author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: The files check partitions stale linked paths by holder lifecycle exactly as dependency_references does, emitting an active count, a legacy closed count, and a legacy terminal count, and it reports status ok when the active partition is empty; The worklist denominator names what it counts: a path count and a link count are separate scalars, the emitted array declares which of the two it is truncating, and no output presents a link-shaped numerator against a path-shaped denominator; One row carries both halves of a repair: for every reported path the holder ids and the inferred destination candidates travel together, so no caller has to join two independently truncated arrays keyed by path; The default summary mode and the verbose mode differ only in length, never in schema, proven by a test that asserts the same row type in both; A stored link that cannot be a workspace-relative path is classified as malformed and excluded from basename move inference, proven by a negative-control fixture holding a comma-joined multi-path literal and a path-colon-note literal, neither of which may produce a moved classification with a destination; The active partition of the repository tracker stays at zero after the fix, and a newly created open item linking a nonexistent path moves it to one, proving the partition is live rather than hardcoded

message: Acceptance criteria for the holder-lifecycle partition, honest denominators, joined worklist rows, mode-stable schema, and malformed-link exclusion
